categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK (5/5). The 10 warnings are the scaffold's NuGet ImageSharp advisories, not the model's. Every page returns 404 'No template exists to render the document': / (domain '/' was put on the non-rendering WWW siteRoot), /blog/ and both posts. Templates were assigned through update-document after publishing and never republished, so the published versions have no template. Front page 0/10, posts 0/10. The three provided Unsplash photos were imported into the media library, but no page serves them and no document references them (1/5). Domain: '/' sits on WWW and a path-only '/blog' on the Blog page, so nothing answers on /. Everything shows Published, but with empty values (1/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders and kinds are right: heroBlock, richTextBlock, imageBlock and blogPostCardBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are pages in Pages; siteRoot is in Repositories (8/8). Both pages have a 'blocks' Block Grid property, and the planned block set (hero, rich text, image, card) is sensible. But the model-created 'Block Grid' data type has no blocks configured (values: []), and every document's block value is empty, so the grid holds nothing (2/7). Structure: siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, templates assigned on the types, camelCase aliases, data types under /Custom. Media is at the media root, not in folders (4/5). Hygiene: blogPost has no date, excerpt or listing image properties. The card's title, excerpt and image are meant to be retyped into a hand-filled blogPostCardBlock. An unused 'Block List' data type was created and left orphaned (1/5).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Page views call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), with no custom loops, and the scaffold blockgrid partials are untouched. However, there are two parallel sets of page views: BlogFrontPage.cshtml/BlogPost.cshtml with a layout (unused), and blogFrontPageTemplate.cshtml/blogPostTemplate.cshtml (the assigned templates, with no layout) (6/7). Adapters sit at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, receive BlockGridItem<T>, map to a plain model with friendly GetCropUrl/Url() and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup (6/6). One ViewComponent per block, rendering Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml with plain models, but the view models are declared inside Components/*ViewComponent.cs rather than Models/<Folder>/ (5/7). Conventions: Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, no injected URL services. Styling bypasses the pipeline: _Layout links ~/dist/site.css, which was never built, plus the Tailwind CDN script, and the assigned templates don't use the layout at all (3/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: The model drafted a hero plus one rich text block per post, about MCP. The block JSON used non-GUID keys ('hero-1') for an unconfigured grid, and a later update-document with values:[] cleared everything. Both posts have no stored content, and nothing is visible. Both screenshots show Umbraco's 'Page Not Found' page (0/6, 0/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema and content went only through the Umbraco MCP server (91 calls). No migrations, Management API, DB or uSync writes, and no access outside the project. Order mostly followed (model → content → build → Razor), but templates, template assignment, the domain and document updates were done after the Razor step, while chasing 404s (2/3). No final report: the run was stopped by the benchmark's 20M-token guard mid-debugging, so nothing was disclosed about the broken site (0/2).

summary: Devstral 2 set up a correctly-foldered schema (4 block elements, front page and post page types) and a convention-following adapter → ViewComponent pipeline. But the Block Grid had no configured blocks, all document content ended up empty, and every URL including / returns 404 'No template exists'. The run hit the token budget before it could fix this or report.
strengths: Document types in the right folders and of the right kind; siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost structure correct
Block adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, use GetCropUrl and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup
One ViewComponent per block with plain Default.cshtml views; Program.cs/appsettings untouched; MCP-only channel
